Title: TELUS streaming telemetry
One line: Network health data in 5 seconds instead of 30+ minutes.
Objective: TELUS home network devices reported their health every 30+ minutes, so problems showed up long after customers felt them. The goal: near real-time telemetry, rolled out to every device.
What I did: Built a Go streaming pipeline on gRPC/gNMI that cut telemetry latency from 30+ min to 5 s across 35+ metrics.
Cross-compiled a Go gNMI agent and deployed it to every OpenWrt arm64 device with a parallel SSH rollout and procd.
Built a Docker ML anomaly pipeline, projected to mean 47% fewer support tickets and $250K/yr in avoided truck rolls.
Caught schema regressions before staging with 6,500+ property-based tests on 51 API operations (Schemathesis).
Stress-tested micro-DPU fiber extender provisioning under peak traffic with load-generation scripts.
Wrote the architecture docs, incident runbook and readiness gaps so operations could take it over.
Calculations:
? speed-up
30+ min ≥ 1800 s → 5 s
1800 / 5 = [[360×]] ✓

? test coverage
6 500 ÷ 51 ops
≈ [[127 tests / op]] ✓
Chart caption: Telemetry latency before and after, same scale
Keywords: streaming telemetry, distributed systems, test automation, anomaly detection, Agile team
Skills used: Go · Docker · gRPC / gNMI streaming · Grafana dashboards · Linux (OpenWrt, arm64) · Property-based API testing · Load and stress testing · Distributed systems · ML anomaly detection · Agile and Jira · Code and design reviews · Docs and incident runbooks

Title: Wingman
One line: Driver-assist that keeps its safety alerts alive even if the AI crashes.
Objective: Driver-assist perception runs on a GPU, and GPUs can hang. Wingman keeps the safety alerts on a separate microcontroller, so a perception fault can never silence them.
What I did: Split the system in two: Jetson GPU perception, and an NXP i.MX RT1170 microcontroller that owns the alerts.
Wrote a CUDA Kalman tracker bank with one thread per tracked object.
Compared array-of-structs and coalesced struct-of-arrays memory layouts on the GPU.
Guaranteed a failsafe within 100 ms of perception loss with a CRC-16 UDP protocol and a Zephyr RTOS state machine.
Calculations:
? why struct-of-arrays
1 warp = 32 threads, each reads one float
32 × 4 B = [[128 B]] in one contiguous read
~ array-of-structs spreads the same reads out

? deadline
t_{failsafe} − t_{last heartbeat}
≤ [[100 ms]] ✓
Chart caption: Timing: perception dies, the failsafe takes over within 100 ms
Other tools: Zephyr RTOS · i.MX RT1170 · UDP · CRC-16
Keywords: safety-critical design, GPU computing, real-time systems, object tracking
Skills used: C++ · Python · CUDA · Zephyr RTOS · Safety state machines · NVIDIA Jetson · GPU memory optimization

Title: SignalScout
One line: A pocket RF tool that replaces 4+ separate field instruments.
Objective: Radio field work means carrying a different tool for every job. SignalScout puts them in one pocket device that can sit on standby for a week.
What I did: Integrated LoRa, GNSS, NFC and an RF detector on a custom Arduino UNO Q shield.
Building off-grid SOS, Wi-Fi/Bluetooth scanning and hidden-camera detection.
Targeting week-long standby by power-gating everything around the STM32WL.
Used Claude Code agents to speed up firmware, PCB and CAD work: drivers, design scripts and tests.

Title: RISC-V SoC + GPU
One line: My own RISC-V CPU and a small graphics accelerator, on an FPGA.
Objective: Learn computer architecture by building it: a RISC-V core written from scratch, grown into a full system-on-chip with video and audio.
What I did: Building an RV32I core in VHDL and extending it into a full SoC on a Tang Nano 9K FPGA.
Fitting a fixed-point Mandelbrot accelerator into 20 hardware multipliers by pipelining the datapath.
Writing bare-metal C firmware and memory-mapped I/O drivers, with HDMI video and PWM audio output.
Calculations:
? one Mandelbrot step
z ← z² + c
(x + iy)² = x² − y² + 2ixy
multiplies: x·x, y·y, x·y = [[3]]
~ 20 multipliers ÷ 3 → at most 6 steps in flight
Chart caption: Multiplier budget for the Mandelbrot accelerator
Other tools: Yosys · Gowin FPGA · HDMI · PWM audio
Keywords: computer architecture, RTL design, FPGA, bare-metal firmware
Skills used: C · VHDL · Bare-metal C drivers (memory-mapped I/O) · FPGA (Gowin, Xilinx) · RTL design · Fixed-point pipelines
